title: Standing-Order Series Routes: Trip Pricing on Mobile In-Home Collection Visits
content:
Route planning questions and answers — **Specimen Collection Appointments**, Mobile In-Home Collection Visit.

**What is the series route?** A home visit collecting a standing order rides the series route. Whether the order is a standing order, and how many test charges have been posted on it, are read from the order's records in Laboratory Test Orders: the order's standing-order flag and the test charge lines posted on its ledger in the last six months.

**How is the trip priced on the series route?** By the number of test charges posted on the standing order in the last six months, applied to the trip's pricing band (the zone band at which the home trip is priced on its appointment date):

| The order | Test charges posted on it in the last six months | Band fee of the trip |
|---|---|---|
| Standing order | Six or more | The fee of the band one nearer than the pricing band, never nearer than service zone 1 |
| Standing order | Three to five | The average of the pricing band's fee and the fee of the band one nearer |
| Standing order | Fewer than three | The fee of the pricing band |
| Not a standing order | Any number | The fee of the pricing band |

**What are the band fees?** The published trip fees: 75.00 for service zone 1, 95.00 for service zone 2, 125.00 for service zone 3. The band one nearer than zone 3 is zone 2; one nearer than zone 2 is zone 1; zone 1 has no nearer band, so it stays at zone 1.

**What do the figures come to?**

| Pricing band | Six or more charges (standing order) | Three to five charges (standing order) | Otherwise |
|---|---|---|---|
| Service zone 1 | 75.00 | 75.00 (average of 75.00 and 75.00) | 75.00 |
| Service zone 2 | 75.00 | 85.00 (average of 95.00 and 75.00) | 95.00 |
| Service zone 3 | 95.00 | 110.00 (average of 125.00 and 95.00) | 125.00 |

**Does a large order that is not a standing order ride the series route?** No. A one-time order with eight test charges posted is priced at the fee of its pricing band.

**Where do the edges fall?** Exactly six charges belong to the six-or-more row; exactly three and exactly five belong to the three-to-five row; two charges fall outside both rows.
